S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

info.persona: William Timana is a methodical, solitary thinker who channels a lifelong respect for community and tradition into disciplined policing, careful budgeting, and a quiet passion for model airplanes and desert photography, even as worry sometimes shadows their calm, and they strive to maintain order in every aspect of life.
info.professional_persona: William Timana, a 57‑year‑old seasoned law‑enforcement officer in Bakersfield, blends three decades of front‑line experience with a humanities degree to excel in forensic investigations, bilingual community outreach, and meticulous patrol protocol development, and they now seek a senior advisory role to embed trauma‑informed, bilingual practices into the department’s curriculum, leveraging their organized, cooperative nature.
info.cultural_background: William was born and raised in Bakersfield to Mexican immigrant parents, growing up in a bilingual household where Spanish and English were spoken interchangeably. His family celebrated Mexican holidays such as Día de los Muertos, Cinco de Mayo, and Semana Santa, while also participating in local Californian traditions. This bicultural upbringing fostered a deep respect for ‘respeto’ and community solidarity, values he carries into his policing career. He is fluent in Spanish, which enables him to communicate effectively with the city’s sizable Latino population and to serve as a cultural liaison within the department. William’s love for traditional Mexican food, music, and storytelling remains a central part of his identity, and he often shares these traditions with colleagues and neighbors as a bridge between cultures.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his downtime, William favors solitary, contemplative activities that align with his preference for quiet environments. He is an avid reader of Mexican literature, U.S. history, and philosophy, often delving into works by Juan Rulfo or Howard Zinn. He builds detailed model airplanes, a hobby that satisfies his need for precision and patience. Photography of the high-desert landscapes around Kern County offers him a way to capture calm moments. William maintains a modest herb and chili garden, using fresh produce in the traditional Mexican dishes he loves to prepare. He also enjoys chess, crossword puzzles, and sudoku, all of which keep his mind sharp while providing a low-stress outlet.
info.sports_persona: William Timana maintains fitness through early morning walks at the Bakersfield Senior Fitness Center, joins a low‑impact cycling group on weekends, and passionately follows the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Bakersfield Condors, and they treat occasional game outings as modest rewards for disciplined routine.
info.arts_persona: William Timana, an avid reader of Juan Rulfo and Howard Zinn, finds solace in photographing high‑desert landscapes in the style of Ansel Adams, enjoys listening to traditional folk ballads and the classical guitar interpretations of songs popularized by Los Tigres del Norte, and they occasionally attend local theater productions of Octavio Paz’s works, discussing the performances with fellow enthusiasts.
info.travel_persona: William Timana prefers meticulously planned road trips, favoring scenic drives through the California desert to Sedona and the Grand Canyon, weekend escapes to the coastal cliffs of Monterey, and a long‑awaited pilgrimage to Oaxaca’s culinary festivals, always budgeting travel expenses to keep their schedule predictable and stress‑free, and they ensure each itinerary aligns with their desire for low‑stress travel.
info.culinary_persona: William Timana, an accomplished home cook, regularly prepares slow‑cooked carnitas, chiles rellenos stuffed with fresh jalapeños from their herb and chili garden, and a hearty pozole broth enriched with hominy and cilantro, balancing modest culinary skill with a love for authentic, spice‑laden family recipes, and they often share the meals during community gatherings.

info.persona: Maria Ruiz is a routine‑loving, bilingual facilities expert who blends a competitive edge in dominoes with a calm, solution‑focused work ethic, cherishes traditional music and cooking, and navigates retirement planning with frugal pragmatism while occasionally letting disorganization slip through.
info.professional_persona: Maria Ruiz has spent decades mastering the practical skills needed to keep large commercial facilities clean and safe, excelling in systematic floor care, industrial equipment operation, OSHA chemical safety compliance, and minor repairs; they now channel their routine‑driven mindset and calm, solution‑focused approach toward earning a facilities‑manager certification and stepping into a supervisory role, while occasionally juggling the disorganized habit of misplacing inventory paperwork.
info.cultural_background: Maria’s cultural identity is rooted in her Puerto Rican heritage, which she maintains through language, food, and festive celebrations. She grew up speaking Spanish at home and learned English after moving to New York as a teenager, making her fully bilingual. Family gatherings are marked by salsa music, holiday dishes, and the observance of traditions such as Noche Buena and the Three Kings Day parade. Though she lives in upstate New York, she stays connected with the local Puerto Rican community through church groups, cultural festivals, and the occasional visit to family on the island. Her Catholic faith, respect for elders, and strong sense of familial duty reflect the values typical of her cultural background.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Maria finds comfort in routines that connect her to her Puerto Rican roots and her rural New York home. She loves preparing traditional dishes like arroz con gandules and empanadillas, often sharing them at family gatherings. Gardening is a daily ritual; she tends a modest vegetable plot, enjoying the predictable cycles of planting, watering, and harvesting. She also knits and crochets blankets using classic patterns, a hobby that satisfies her love of orderly, tactile projects. On weekends she joins a local domino club, where her competitive streak shines, and she occasionally attends the nearby Catholic church for services and community events. Walking along the shores of Ballston Lake provides a peaceful solitary escape.
info.sports_persona: Maria Ruiz enjoys a steady fitness routine that combines daily walks around Ballston Lake with cheering on the Buffalo Bills during football season and the New York Rangers in winter, and on weekends they compete fiercely at the local domino club where strategic thinking feels like a mental sport, though their competitive edge contrasts with a laid‑back schedule when it comes to formal exercise classes.
info.arts_persona: Maria Ruiz finds artistic fulfillment in the rhythms of salsa music that fill family celebrations, the timeless performances of Rita Moreno and the classic films of the Golden Age, and the tactile creativity of crocheting and knitting blankets with traditional patterns, often humming along to Celia Cruz while crafting, and occasionally joining the church choir to lift their voice in harmonious worship.
info.travel_persona: Maria Ruiz’s travel style blends spontaneous weekend getaways to nearby lakeside cabins with well‑planned pilgrimages to the island for the Three Kings Day parade, and they daydream about a leisurely cruise to the Caribbean after retirement, balancing a modest travel budget with a desire to reconnect with extended family and the soothing sound of ocean waves.
info.culinary_persona: Maria Ruiz delights in preparing arroz con gandules with a simmering sofrito of onions, garlic, cilantro, and annatto, and hand‑folding empanadillas stuffed with seasoned ground beef and olives, frequently seasoning dishes with a pinch of adobo and a squeeze of lime; they are a confident home cook who often gathers friends for a feast, yet their tendency to linger on TV commercials sometimes leaves the rice a little too soft.

info.persona: Jesus Reyes balances firefighting precision with a laid‑back love of vintage bikes, hikes, acoustic guitar jam sessions, and Mexican‑inspired cooking, all while staying skeptical of shortcuts and quietly competitive in both work and play, and they approach each challenge with a calm, improvisational mindset.
info.professional_persona: Jesus Reyes, a 27‑year‑old firefighter in Beloit, blends their practical expertise in fire suppression, EMT‑B care, and hazardous‑materials identification with a curiosity for emerging tech like drones and thermal imaging, improvising solutions on the fireground while they pursue certifications and a future as a lieutenant and training officer.
info.cultural_background: Jesus grew up in a bicultural Mexican‑American household in the Midwest. His parents immigrated from Jalisco and instilled strong family values, bilingual fluency in Spanish and English, and a deep respect for Mexican traditions. He participates regularly in local Latino community events, attends Mass, and celebrates Mexican holidays such as Día de los Muertos and Christmas with his wife and extended family. The blend of Mexican heritage and Midwestern life shapes his worldview, informing his community‑oriented approach as a firefighter and his pride in sharing cultural traditions with neighbors in Beloit.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his downtime, Jesus balances solo reflection with social connection. He enjoys hiking the nearby Kettle Moraine State Forest, fishing on Lake Winnebago, and restoring a vintage motorcycle, satisfying his curiosity about mechanical systems. Music is a big part of his life; he plays acoustic guitar and often jams with friends at local gatherings. He stays connected to his Mexican roots by cooking traditional dishes, celebrating Día de los Muertos, and participating in the annual Mexican cultural festival in Beloit. Occasionally, he channels his competitive streak through online multiplayer video games and watches fire‑science documentaries.
info.sports_persona: Jesus Reyes stays fit by hiking the Kettle Moraine State Forest in summer, fishing on Lake Winnebago in spring, playing pickup basketball with friends while cheering the Milwaukee Bucks, and volunteering with the local soccer league, all while they maintain a casual gym routine that balances their love of outdoor adventure with the need for stamina on the fireground.
info.arts_persona: Jesus Reyes, an acoustic‑guitar enthusiast, regularly jams with friends at local gatherings, draws inspiration from John Mayer’s fingerstyle, the folk‑rock of Mumford & Sons, and classic corridos by Vicente Fernández, and they spend evenings watching fire‑science documentaries that blend their profession with a love of storytelling.
info.travel_persona: Jesus Reyes prefers spontaneous road‑trip adventures, often planning weekend escapes to Door County or the Upper Peninsula, has explored Oaxaca’s street food, trekked the Grand Canyon, and dreams of backpacking Patagonia, balancing their love of nature with budget‑friendly travel and occasional flights to visit family during Día de los Muertos, and they always keep a spare map in their truck for unplanned detours.
info.culinary_persona: Jesus Reyes enjoys cooking traditional dishes such as tamales, carnitas, and chiles en nogada on their grill, pairs them with craft beers from local breweries, and though their culinary skills are solid, they often improvise recipes with whatever ingredients are on hand, reflecting their flexible mindset.
